utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody, even though it is not a very good afternoon because Judge Schomburg has taken ill. May I ask the Registrar to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And appearances for the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Lotte Karlsson for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Branko Lukic and John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. And as I just told, Judge Schomburg is unfortunately not available to sit in the courtroom this afternoon because he is not well. I understand from the legal officer that she has informed you of his unavailability and that there are no objections to Judge Argibay and I sitting this afternoon under Rule 15 bis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Defence does not have any objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask, Dr. Stakic, do you have any objections to proceeding in this way?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Therefore, considering that Judge Schomburg is not available to sit in this case today for reasons of his personal health, Judge Argibay and I, being satisfied that it is in the interest of the justice to do so, and based on the consent of the parties and Dr. Stakic himself, I hereby order pursuant to Rule 15 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence that for today, the hearing continue in the absence of Judge Schomburg. I would like to start with -- I would like to touch upon some procedural matters. As regards today's witness, in light of Judge Schomburg's absence, I would like to ask the parties whether they object to interrupting the testimony of Mr. Travar, who is appearing as Chamber witness, in order to hear Defence Witness 043?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. As we shared with the Court officer this morning, we are of the position that 043 is not prepared since we did not meet with him at length and scheduled to meet with him this evening and tomorrow morning as well, as we have indicated to the Victim and Witness Unit. So we would not be prepared to proceed with Witness Number 043 at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But as far as I remember, the Witness 043 had to be ready to testify last week, on Thursday or Friday. And we got a proffer for the testimony of this witness, and I don't understand why it is impossible to start with Witness 043 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, I could explain that to Your Honours. The witness arrived, I believe, last Thursday afternoon at The Hague. We spent that evening obtaining general information for the proffer. We did not cover the specific documents we wanted to with the witness. In the interim, as the Court recalls. The schedule of the witness who testified, Mr. Budimir, lasted far longer, and we had another witness in the dock that we were meeting with and preparing. So we spent the Thursday with that witness as well as Friday preparing the witness who the Court heard, 006, on Friday. Subsequent to that, we were preparing since Mr. Travar started his testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: -- Our schedule indicated that he would be proceeding after Mr. Travar. So we allowed him to relax since he just travelled here, and we did not want to tax him in terms of all the documents --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Was calculate and since we were not advised of it since until morning and we were present for the 65 ter conference that was cancelled obviously, we did not schedule to meet with him and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... We would meet with him on Monday evening and Tuesday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But long before last week, the Chamber asked for Witness 043 to be prepared for testimony on Thursday. That's why we would prefer to start with Witness 043, to save the time and to meet the emergency related to the illness of Judge Schomburg. And it is difficult to understand why this witness wasn't prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, first of all, the witness was scheduled -- was supposed to come earlier but only arrived Thursday afternoon. As the Court knows, we sat Thursday as well as Friday, so we could not meet with him to prepare him, other than in the evening hours. Secondly, we had a second witness, 006, who was testifying, and we needed to meet and prepare that witness for his testimony on Friday. Similarly, on Friday afternoon, Mr. Travar was called to the stand, and started testifying. Had we known -- obviously it's something that happened late in the weekend if not this morning. Had we known, we would have started, and if the Court instructed us to bring the witness for Monday, we would have had him prepared this weekend. We were busy doing an enormous of other things -- and I apologise for that for the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Again, I remind you that the Bench ordered Witness 043 to be prepared to testify for Thursday last week, and it was scheduled. So that's why we hoped that this witness will be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court remembers, on the record, we even said we were placed in a catch-22 for the witness to have testified on Thursday, we had not met with him until Thursday evening. It would have been impossible. We shared that early on with the Court. So I think initially, we had anticipated based on the schedule that the witness would arrive sooner and that based on the time schedule, he would be prepared to testify on Thursday or Friday. But as the week progressed, everything changed and left us in ultimately a state of confusion because of these witnesses. So again, we apologise to the Court. But the witness is not prepared, and if someone would have called us sooner, we would have attempted to prepare him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... Be prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The witness, as I stated earlier, we are meeting with him this evening at 7.30 as well as tomorrow at 9.00. He could proceed to be ready by tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. After consulting with Judge Argibay, the Chamber rules as follows: The Chamber decided to proceed today with Mr. Travar only in the absence of Judge Schomburg in the Court. After questions from the Bench, please do -- well, some procedural issues. After questions from the Bench, the Defence will have an opportunity to put their questions to Mr. Travar, followed by the Prosecution. This, of course, will not prejudice the right of either party to put questions to Mr. Travar following any additional questions from the Bench tomorrow. Therefore, we shall now continue with the evidence of Mr. Travar. Could the usher please bring the witness in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Travar. The Bench would like to remind you that you are still under solemn declaration to tell the truth in this courtroom. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Perhaps the Defence [sic] explained to you that today we have the hearings in the compositions two Judges because Judge Schomburg has taken ill. And acting in accordance to the Rules of Procedures, we will proceed in the limited composition. On Friday afternoon, Judge Schomburg questioned you about the events of the night of 29th April, 1992, in Prijedor. In your effort to a meeting that took place in Cirkin Polje, attended by, among others, what you described as members of the new Executive Board. I would refer the parties to the pages 13.244, 13.246 of Friday's transcript. My first line of questioning relate to the events of this evening. And in this regard, I would like the audiobooth to play an audiotape, Exhibit S91. Mr. Travar, this exhibit purports to be a transcript of a broadcast of Radio Prijedor in 1995 entitled "Remembering the takeover." I would ask that you, Mr. Travar, listen carefully to the tape and indicate when you have any comments or when you recognise any of the voices on the tape. After the tape has finished, I will put some questions to you. And when you will recognise the voices, please to say "stop," and then comment. Could the audiobooth please play the tape, Exhibit S91, as cued.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. This is Mr. Miskovic's voice. But first, I'd like to say that you began by saying that the Defence had told me what would happen today. But I did not communicate with the Defence because I'm the witness of the Court. So I wanted to make this clear. I did not communicate with the Defence. However, this is Mr. Miskovic's voice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please -- audiobooth, please, to continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. This is the voice of Zivko Ecim, the reporter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And Zivko Ecim mentioned the name of Simo Drljaca. Was it the voice of Simo Miskovic or Simo Drljaca?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the voice of Simo Miskovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us continue with the tape.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stop. This was the voice of Mr. Kuruzovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please do continue playing the tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Stop. This concludes this part of the audiotape. My question to you, Mr. Travar, having heard this : Do you have any amendments to your testimony of Friday, especially related to the meeting in Cirkin Polje?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have never heard of this tape before. You said that this tape was recorded in 1995. In that period, in 1992, I was not informed about many of the things which are mentioned on this tape. It was sometime in late March that I was informed by the then president of the party, and I believe that it was Mr. Miskovic. He informed me that I am supposed to come to this meeting. I believe that it was the meeting of the SDS board. At that time, I was not a member of the party, and I didn't participate in any of these activities. What I know for a fact is that after midnight, two policemen came to fetch me, because in the meantime, on the 16th of April, at the session of the assembly, a new Executive Board had been appointed. And that's how I found myself in Cirkin Polje. As for all the events that preceded that moment, I claim with full responsibility that I didn't know anything about those events nor did I have an opportunity to listen to this interview that was conducted with Mr. Miskovic and Mr. Kuruzovic. What I know for a fact is that here, the Crisis Staff is mentioned. The Crisis Staff at that time did not exist. It was established in mid-May pursuant to the instruction of the presidency, or maybe it was in late May, in the latter part of May. And this happened at one of the sessions, and then it was that the functions were established that would later on form the Crisis Staff. Here, when they talk about the Crisis Staff, I did not attend any of the meetings before the 16th of April. I didn't participate in any of the meetings, and I was not aware of any of the meetings that took place in the afternoon in the barracks and elsewhere, as it is mentioned on this tape. My first information about the takeover and about our departure for the assembly building -- I learned my first information about that when I arrived in Cirkin Polje after midnight. I don't have any other comments because at that time, I was not an active member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar, for your answer. My next question: What was Dr. Stakic's position after the takeover?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dr. Stakic was appointed as the president of the Municipal Assembly. He was appointed at the session which was held sometime in mid-April. From then onwards, he was the president of the Municipal Assembly, from the 16th of April, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But as far as I understand, at that time, the president of the Municipal Assembly was Dr. Cehajic.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my testimony on Friday, I tried to explain the situation as much as I was informed about it. And my information all came from the media. There was a rift among the deputies in the state assembly, and this had a ripple effect on the deputies in Municipal Assemblies. The deputies of the Serbian ethnicity decided to establish a Serbian Assembly. I know that Dr. Cehajic was the president of the municipality. He was elected after the first multiparty election. I believe that it was in 1991, but I'm not sure of that. I believe that Dr. Stakic at that time was his deputy during that period of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And after the takeover, Dr. Stakic became --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the takeover, Dr. Stakic became the president of the Serbian Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Of the Serbian Municipal Assembly. Yes. And what was the fate of --

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, the Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: In your municipality. And what was the powers of Dr. Stakic as president of the municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must be honest and say that I was not familiar with the structure and the legislative power and administration. So I wouldn't be able to tell you anything about the powers that he had. I know that he chaired the assembly meetings and that he had some duties within the municipality. He chaired the sessions, and the Municipal Assembly would adopt decisions proposed by Dr. Stakic as the president. And when the decisions were passed, he would sign those decisions. I'm not that familiar with this part of the legislative power, and I therefore can't give you any details on his powers at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was Dr. Stakic an influential political figure in the municipality and as president of the Municipal Assembly?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can tell you at this moment is that Dr. Stakic was young Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. and not experienced enough to be the leading political figure. There were many more people who were much better known than him. It was a well-known fact that he was the president of the Municipal Assembly, and that is what I also could learn from the media. But I don't think that he played a significant political role at that moment given his age and his experience. I wouldn't say that he was a prominent politician.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And how can you explain the fact that Dr. Stakic, being young, inexperienced politician, was elected as the president of the Municipal Assembly -- vice-president of Municipal Assembly, and then was, after the takeover, was appointed as the president of the assembly while in the Prijedor Municipality there were other more influential and prominent political figures?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't comment on that. I didn't participate in the interparty negotiations after the elections because I was not politically engaged in any of the parties. So I really don't know how it happened that a person who didn't have any political experience was appointed. I believe it was some sort of a compromise between the political parties, but I can't give you any comments because at that time I wasn't there and I was not a member of any of the political structures. So I can't give you any personal opinion on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you. My following question: You mentioned that the Crisis Staff was set up later in May 1992. When exactly and why a Crisis Staff was created and replaced the Municipal Assembly, legitimate body?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the reasons why it happened. But I do know that pursuant to the instruction issued by the then-presidency of the republic -- the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina - I believe that this was the full title of the state - an instruction came in which it said that the Municipal Assembly couldn't meet because of the conditions of an immediate threat of war, and that the Municipal Assemblies should be replaced by the Crisis Staffs that would meet instead of Municipal Assemblies. After that, there was a decision issued by the then-government of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and this decision provided for the work of that body prescribing the functions and bodies that would constitute the Crisis Staff. I really don't know what the reasons were for the establishment of the Crisis Staff because at that moment when the Crisis Staff was set up in Prijedor, there were no war operations going on. I believe that this was sometime around the 20th of May. In any case, in the latter part of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did you take part in the setting up of the Crisis Staff in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I? The Crisis Staff was appointed by the Municipal Assembly pursuant to the instruction that was issued by either the presidency or the government of the then-Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And this instruction prescribed the sectors that would constitute the Crisis Staff. And the Crisis Staff was appointed by the Municipal Assembly. And yes, I believe that I did participate at that session of the Municipal Assembly, which was held in the latter part of May, but I can't be sure of that. I know that my secretariat, the secretariat that I later on headed, was one part of that Crisis Staff pursuant to the instruction of the presidency of the republic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And did you participate personally in meetings related to the -- which -- where the establishment or setting up of the Crisis Staff were discussed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't participate in these meetings. As the secretary of the secretariat -- I don't know. Which meetings do you have in mind? But in any case, as the secretary of the secretariat which covered a very delicate area, and those were budget and finances, I was invited to a number of meetings, and I participated as the secretary of that secretariat in a number of meetings. But I don't know what meetings do you have in mind in terms of the establishment of the Crisis Staff? I know that the Crisis Staff was established by the Municipal Assembly pursuant to the instruction issued by the then-presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: May I ask usher to show the witness Exhibit S60. May I ask the witness to read out the first page of this document.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipality held on 15 May 1992 starting at 1000 hours. Dr. Milomir Stakic president of the council chaired the meeting." Do I have to repeat what I've just read?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: No, please do continue reading.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The meeting was attended by the following: Dr. Milomir Stakic, Dr. Milan Kovacevic, Simo Miskovic, Vladimir Arsic, Pero Colic, Slobodan Kuruzovic, Radmilo Zeljaja, Rade Javoric, Slavko Budimir, Simo Drljaca, Cedo Sipovac, Vojo Pavicic, Bosko Mandic, Ranko Travar, Milenko Rajlic, Dragan Savanovic. Spiro Marmat kept the minutes. The following agenda was confirmed: 1, decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff. 2" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Stop. Then please point to 1 of the agenda on the following part.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The decision on the organisation and the functioning of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do continue.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Shall I continue or do you want me to comment on this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do read out to the end of this page, and then please do comment.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "2, mobilisation in the municipality. 3, the issue of the status of deployed forces. 4, disarmament of paramilitary formations. 5, taking over the duties of the military department. "Item 1, the decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff, the following persons participated in the discussion: Milomir Stakic and Slavko Budimir. After the discussion, the following conclusion was reached: Under 1, "It is hereby accepted to organise and start the function of the Crisis Staff. The proposed composition of the Crisis Staff shall be supplemented by the -- by a representative of the Prijedor Garrison. "2" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Stop. That's enough. Now, please do comment. You would like to make some comments, please.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just say that in my testimony last year, as a witness for the Prosecution, I said that I did not remember this body or this organ, nor do I know what its role was, that is, the National Defence council. There were some specific questions put to me, and I said that I did not remember the National Defence Council, and that I didn't know what its authorities were. I also don't know how it was set up, how it was established. I attended a number of meetings, not only this one, and probably because of the specificity of my job. Here, I can see that I was present at this meeting, that I attended this meeting, but I have forgotten what was discussed at all of these meetings. And as for this meeting, if I participated in the discussion, it was only about the issues that pertained to the purview of my secretariat, and it was my duty to exempt the -- some of the people from the military mobilisation in order to enable the companies in Prijedor to keep on functioning. I wanted to see Prijedor being supplied with electricity, water, food. I wanted the town to prepare for the harvest, and that's why it was my duty to exempt as many military conscripts as possible from serving in the units. And that is the only thing that I could talk about at this meeting, and that is why I can't remember this particular body. I don't know what its main task was, what its essence was, and I don't know what kind of decisions it could make. I have never seen these minutes before -- I may have seen it if Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the Prosecution showed it to me during my previous testimony, but I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, I am not asking you about the council for people's defence. I'm asking you about the Crisis Staff. And that's why this -- the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is not a standard, normal issue which were discussed. It is an extraordinary issue. And that's why I am asking you: Do you remember what was going on at that time and how the Crisis Staff was set up? You were a member of the Crisis Staff. And how the other people were appointed to the Crisis Staff? Did military and police take part in the Crisis Staff, as members or as invited persons?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police did have a representative in the Crisis Staff, but the army didn't. And he was never appointed by the Municipal Assembly as a member of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Who is "he"? You said: "He was never appointed as a member of the Crisis Staff." Who is "he"?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: A representative of the army. No representatives of the army were appointed as a member of the Crisis Staff because that would be contrary to the instruction on the establishment of Crisis Staffs at municipality level.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But in the document you just have read, it is said that the people's defence council recommended that the representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of members of the Crisis Staff. Do you remember that? Do you remember who made this proposal?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, Your Honour. I only know that an army representative, a garrison representative, was never appointed as a member of the Crisis Staff. No army representative ever participated in the meetings of the Crisis Staff as a member. And who it was who proposed this at this particular meeting, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You just said that representatives of the military never participated in the functioning of the Crisis Staff as a member. But did the military be represented -- did the military attend the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very rarely. But only when they wished to attend those meetings and when solutions were sought for their materiel status. For example, when we discussed problems that culminated in terms of the supply of the army with food, first and foremost. And also when there were requests for some of the conscripts who had been mobilised to be released from the units, they were invited only as guests to those meetings. It happened very rarely. I attended a few meetings which were attended by the military who participated in the discussion of the issues that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. It seems to me it is an appropriate time to have a break. The trial stays adjourned until 4.15 [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, let's continue. My next question: How were people appointed to the Crisis Staff? What were the criteria for appointment the members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the criteria were. But I know there was a decision, whether of the presidency or of the government, on that basis of which people were appointed -- they were appointments by function. That is, not the names, but the functions were the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues]... Did you were appointed as member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on the basis of the criteria laid down by either the government or the presidency of the then-republic, it was said that the secretariat for economics and services activities should also be incorporated, and I headed it. Had it been somebody else, it wouldn't be so. It was the office that I held that made me a member of the Crisis Staff, not my name, not I as a person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do you remember the names of the other members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll do my best to recall them. I do remember most of them, but perhaps I'll omit a name or two. Ex officio members were the president of the assembly and the president of the board. And those were Mr. Kovacevic -- Mr. Stakic and Mr. Kovacevic. Then their deputies, Mr. Mandic and Mr. Savanovic. The secretary for National Defence, it was Mr. Budimir. Secretariat for property affairs, Mr. Pavicic. The secretariat for economics and finance, that is budget and finance, it was myself. Then I think that the secretary for information or a person responsible for information was -- I think it was Milenko Rajlic, also was a member of the Crisis Staff. But there is a decision which specified the offices and the names of the members of the Crisis Staff. So that at present, I can't remember any more, either offices or names. But there is a decision with the exact offices and names of people who made up the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What about the representative of the police?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise. Yes. A representative of the police, Mr. Simo Drljaca, who was the chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: How long was the Crisis Staff in existence?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. But I think it was until July or mid-July. It worked for about two, two and a half months. I can't remember the date when it was abolished. I also believe there is a decision on its dissolution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was it always called the "Crisis Staff"?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean, during that period of time was it called that? Yes, it was called the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Have you heard the name "war presidency" or "war commission"?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with that term. But I do not think that at that time there was anything like that. I believe that later on -- the war commission or the war presidency was set up later on. But I don't think that at the time of the Crisis Staff, such a body existed, and I do not know who it consisted of. No, I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So in your opinion, the Crisis Staff was renamed at one point of time as war presidency or as war commission?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the war commission was set up following the Crisis Staff, because that was not my job, and I believe the people in the professional bodies of the Municipal Assembly would know that. I just can't remember. I know that the term "war presidency" rings a bell, but whether it immediately -- it came -- it emerged in the wake of the Crisis Staff or not, I simply can't confirm that. And I do not know who were its members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. My next question: Who was the president of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Crisis Staff was the president of the assembly ex officio, and that was Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So Mr. Stakic became president of the Crisis Staff ex officio; he wasn't elected as such at the first meeting of the Crisis Staff? Or he was elected?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And who presided over the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, it was Mr. Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And when Mr. Stakic was absent, who was presiding over the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was Mr. Kovacevic who did that. But at times, the vice-president of the assembly, Mr. Savanovic, was in the chair. But more often than not, it would be Mr. Kovacevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So either Mr. Kovacevic or Mr. Savanovic presided over the Crisis Staff when Mr. Stakic was absent. Yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, but it was Mr. Kovacevic as often as not. Of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. course, I have to add that I did not attend all the meetings of the Crisis Staff, that is, I'm referring only to those meetings of the Crisis Staff that I attended. I need to make this reservation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Had you attended -- have you attended the first meeting, the very first meeting of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember, Your Honour. I believe I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And do you remember what issues were discussed during the first meeting of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember. It was 11 years ago, and these are details. Only if I had some documents to look at them, then perhaps I could say something about it. But what were the issues, I really -- I'm not even sure that I -- I'm not even sure that I attended the first meeting of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: The first meeting of such an important body in such a very difficult time in the life of your country and Prijedor Municipality and -- okay. How were the meetings organised? What were the working order of the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be quite honest, I do not think that the way in which meetings were convened was regulated. I think it was professional services, or rather the services of the assembly, because it was practically the assembly which was in session, that is, which was convened because of the assembly could not be convened on a regular basis. And I believe that it was the professional services which prepared and organised the work if the Crisis Staff did not do it properly. The meetings were usually convened ad hoc. Most of them would adopt the agenda after the people had gathered there. And there were no minutes of those meetings and decisions which were related to the Crisis Staff. That is, I would not say that there was a uniform -- I can't say that there was a standard, uniform way in which these things were regulated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And how often the meetings of the Crisis Staff were convened?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, I do not think that they were particularly frequent. I cannot say. They were held when the need arose. So that is when the president would think that there were questions warranting discussion. He would call a meeting and suggest that they be included in the agenda. So I do not know how many meetings were held, but there should be either records or decisions that were adopted there because all the decisions of the Crisis Staff had to be in accordance with a decision of the government of the Serb Republic. Also decisions had to be ratified by the assembly. So that there are those decisions and the dates of their adoption. But I wouldn't be able to say how many sessions there really exactly were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You anticipate that the dates of the adoption of the decisions or enactments of the Crisis Staff are the dates of the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that's how it was. It couldn't be any other way. I mean, I don't know. I really can't -- I didn't run the Crisis Staff, and the secretariat or the legal staff who were to take care of that, they did it so that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit S250. May I ask the witness to read out the first half of this document.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Assembly of the Municipality of Prijedor, confirmation of decisions within the competence of the Municipal Assembly adopted by the Crisis Staff. "At the session of the 20th of May, 1992, the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor adopted decision such and such number on the organisation and work of the Crisis Staff. Article 2 of the above decision lays down that the Crisis Staff shall decide on matters within the jurisdiction of the Municipal Assembly if the assembly cannot meet, but has the duty to submit every decision it adopts for confirmation by the Assembly as soon as the Assembly can meet. By decision number 01-023-53/92, dated 14th July, 1992, the Crisis Staff was renamed the war presidency, retaining the same members and powers. "Between the 29th of May and the 24th of July, 1992, the Crisis Staff -- that is, the war presidency, adopted enactments, decisions, orders, dispositions and conclusions which are hereby submitted to the Assembly for confirmation as follows: "1, enactments of the 29th of May, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Now, please do read out only the titles of the items, first, 2, 3, 4, and following. Okay. The first item, "enactments passed on 29th May, 1992." Yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Item 1, enactments passed on 29th of May, 1992. 2, enactments passed on 31st May, 1992. 1, decision number 2 on the dismissal of the" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: No, no, it's not necessary to read out the names of the decisions. I ask you to read out the -- just the titles of the issues, 1, 2, 3, 4, Roman.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman, I see. So enactments of the 29th of May, 1992. "II enactments of the 31st of May, 1992. III, enactments of the 3rd of June, 1992. IV, enactments of the 4th of June, 1992. V, enactments of the 5th of June, 1992. VI, enactments of the 6th of June, 1992. VII, enactments of the 7th of June, 1992. VIII, enactments of the 8th of June, 1992. IX, enactments of the 10th of June, 1992. X" -- there's something before it, I don't know whether it's 9 or 10, I don't know. "Of the 11th of June, 1992. XI, enactments of the 12th of June, 1992."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Enough. Now, having read the enactments and the titles of the issues from I to X, can you conclude that the meetings of the Crisis Staff took place every day in the first decade of June?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why, yes, often. Now I see between the 5th to the 10th of June, practically every day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What kind of issues were discussed during the meetings of the Crisis Staff during these ten days?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Many issues predominated at those meetings. But by and large, those were issues which had to do with life in the town, that is, the supply of the town. At that time, there were shortages of electricity, of water. I mean, I can remember perhaps the subjects that were of major concern to me as a member of this body, and perhaps say something about them. But 99 per cent of the issues had to do with the operation of some normal life in the town at that time because it was intolerable at the time. So it was the time when there was no electricity, and Prijedor is a town where there is no water if there is no electricity. Basic necessities, and I am now talking about my field of work, so basic foodstuffs were distributed on the basis of lists with the right to introduce coupons, that is, to ration the food. There were also other issues which had to do with the harvest, with sowing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So you're insisting that in time of war, 99 per cent of the issues discussed in the Crisis Staff were related to the normal life? How it come?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the Crisis Staff and municipal agencies by virtue of the laws which governed their work, and neither the Crisis Staff nor the Executive Board changed them. And by statute, they could not discuss matters or put on the agenda matters that fell outside their field of operation. The meetings of the Crisis Staff, I usually took part in discussion which had to do with the attempts to establish normal life in the town, that is, the supply side of the public amenities, social problems, harvest, sowing, and so on and so forth. If military issues, whether they were discussed by the Crisis Staff, if you tried to or if you wanted to -- if you had guests or invited guests or visitors who were military persons, you could never get a valid answer what was going on because they had their own chain of command and reporting. Their answer invariably was "that's none of your business" or something along those Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. lines. "Things are under control." So it was simply impossible to discuss any of such matters with anyone from the ranks of the military. And we knew, I as somebody from the town, was aware of combat operations, that in the town, there were all sorts of things happening, from looting to murders to everything else. But the Crisis Staff could never discuss such matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, as far as I understand, the Crisis Staff was an extraordinary body which was created in the state of emergency. Yes or no? And it was the only body functioning in the Prijedor Municipality at that time.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, yes, this body was set up because the assembly could not meet. And it discussed matters that were within the jurisdiction of the assembly. Which issues those were and what issues the assembly could discuss, I, as a member of the Crisis Staff, that is, as a member of the Executive Board and the secretary of the secretariat, I cannot confirm what were the issues under the -- in the province of the assembly because the secretariat had to bear in mind that every one of those agencies and bodies was adopting decisions falling within their competence. And that was why the Crisis Staff was set up. But again, it could not go beyond its province of work as laid down by the constitution and statute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit S110. May I ask the witness to read out the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pursuant to Article 110 of the Assembly of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor at its session of the 20th of May, adopted the following decision on the organisation of work of the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor. "Pursuant to this decision, the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor is formed and its spere of action set out. "Item 2, the Executive Board [as interpreted] of the Municipality of Prijedor is set up to coordinate work, to provide for the safety of" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Item 2, it seems [No microphone]

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff, this is the decision on the establishment of the Crisis Staff of the Municipal Assembly of the 20th of May, that is. I didn't say the Executive Board. I said the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. On the transcript, it was the Executive Board. That's why I interrupted you. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Prijedor municipal Crisis Staff is established according to the functions of the authorities, the defence of the municipal territory, the protection of safety of people and property, the establishment of government, and the organisation of all other fields of life and work. As coordinator" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Stop. Then I ask you to read out Article 5 of this document.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Article 5: In accordance with the assessment of the political and security situation and realistic requirements, the Crisis Staff shall adopt relevant decisions on the organisation and work of the Municipal Assembly, its organs, and other municipal organs and local communes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So as far as I understand --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: According to the Article 5 of this document, the Crisis Staff has the right and duty to assess the political and security situation, make realistic requirements, and to adopt relevant decisions. Do you remember meetings of the Crisis Staff when political -- assessments of the political and security situation in Prijedor Municipality were discussed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were meetings of the Crisis Staff where items of the agenda were the discussion on the political and security situation in Prijedor. Reports were submitted and read about the situation, and this was usually done by the chair, by the person presiding the meeting. And as for the security situation, I've told you that it was very rarely or almost never that we had enough information from the public security station. Whenever you wanted to ask Mr. Drljaca about the situation, he would reply that this is something that the municipality cannot go into. He said "municipality is one thing, and we have our line of reporting towards the Ministry of the Interior," and that is why these items were rarely put on the agenda of those meetings that I attended. Having said that, I repeat, there were meetings at which these issues were indeed discussed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And what kind of decisions were taken while the questions of -- or issues of the political and security situation were discussed?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour, what decisions you have in mind. We did not adopt any specific decisions. We usually received information, and this information was taken into consideration. But we never adopted any decisions falling under that area. We would never vote on those things. We would never adopt decisions. We're talking more about information, about the number of crimes, traffic accidents, and so on and so forth. But we only received that as information, just information, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Have you ever -- had the Crisis Staff ever discuss the issues related to the armed conflict in the Prijedor Municipality, the establishment of the camps or detention centres in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We never discussed these issues. I've told you. Whenever we wanted to learn something, this was not something that the Crisis Staff would do, and this is the kind of reply we would get. They would tell us: "These are not issues of your concern. Everything is under control." This is the kind of answers we would get from the persons who attended the Crisis Staff meetings as army representatives. But that happened very rarely. At the meetings of the Crisis Staff that I attended, we never discussed these issues, nor could we put these issues on the agenda of our meetings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Did the Crisis Staff discuss the issues related to the incident in Hambarine village?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't attend any such meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: May I ask the usher to show the witness Exhibit S353. Please do read the very beginning of this document.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Ministry of the Interior, Security Services Centre Banja Luka, public security station Prijedor. Official secret. Strictly confidential. "At the request of the commission of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre formed pursuant to the decision of the chief of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre number 11-141/2 of 14 August 1992, Prijedor public security station, in addition to presenting the existing documentation and allowing an insight into the situation in the field, submits to the commission for its use the following report: "1, reception centres in the Municipality of Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please stop. And then the -- please do look at the page 9 of this document. Whose signature is it? Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, Your Honour. It says the chief of the public security station, Simo Drljaca. But I don't know whether this is his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You never saw his signature before?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. Although I saw it, I have recognised signatures that I saw often. But this one, I can't remember. I assume that this will be his signature because it doesn't say here that somebody signed on his behalf. But I cannot remember that this indeed is his signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. Now please do look at the page 2 of this document. Did you find the page?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, page number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please do read out the para 2 of this page. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Since the citizens of the village of Hambarine did not respect the decision of the Ministry of National Defence of the Serbian Republic and did not surrender their arms, they refused to cooperate with the legal organs of government over the attack on the soldiers, and rejected demands the army made to them, the Crisis Staff of the Municipality of Prijedor decided on military intervention in this village to disarm and capture the known perpetrators of the crimes against the soldiers. The army did intervene, but it did not" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Stop. So far as I understand, this document says "the Crisis Staff of the Prijedor Municipality decided to intervene militarily..." How you can comment this part of the document?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am a hundred per cent sure that the Crisis Staff did not adopt this decision. I was not at this session in any case, and this is my only comment, I'm sorry to say. I see this document for the first time. This report was drafted by the ministry and submitted to the public security centre. This is not a report that was commissioned by the Crisis Staff. The essence of the problem is that I am sure -- and when I look at things now, I'm sure that both the army and the police abused the position in the name of the Crisis Staff. And this document confirms it very well and confirms my suspicion about the honesty of the things which were done by the police and the army at that time. And they wanted to pass their acts on as the acts of the Crisis Staff. I'm sure that a decision like that was never adopted at any of the sessions of the Crisis Staff. This is a report that was submitted to the Security Services Centre. I don't even know when this was drafted. If you will allow me a second to look at the date on the document...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please do it.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the date of this report is. It says here that this was done at the request of the Public Security Services Centre, and that the decision was dated 14 August. So this is a request that came from Banja Luka, from the Security Services Centre. And the police had its line of command and the line of reporting. And they were in no way subordinated either to the Crisis Staff or to any other municipal body. That was the case before and it is still the case to this very day. I really can't comment on this document. I can only say with certainty that at the Crisis Staff meetings that I attended, this decision or a decision of that kind was never adopted, and I claim that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Can you tell us who proposed decisions? Who proposed draft decisions? How they were discussed? How they were adopted? What was the voting procedure?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Decisions of the Crisis Staff were not drafted because of the negligence of the technical services of the municipality. They were not drafted in a proper way. They were not worded in the proper way. There was occasional voting at the meetings of the Crisis Staff when there were important issues on the agenda. But the majority of the issues on the agenda were relative to an aspect of the civilian life in the town, and usually the final -- the last sentence was "is there anybody against?" If something was defined as a conclusion or a decision or an order, that would be in keeping with the authorities of the Crisis Staff and could have been adopted as such. I didn't have any feedback in -- either as the minutes of that meeting or the decisions adopted at that meeting. The only decisions I received were those decisions that covered an aspect of the area that my secretariat was in charge of. There was occasional decision-taking by vote at the meetings of the Crisis Staff. Questions would be asked whether there was something against, if an enactment was defined within the purview of the Municipal Assembly and the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But to my knowledge, about texts -- about 200 decisions and other enactments of the Crisis Staff were transferred to the Municipal Assembly for adoption. And you have read the part of the document. And a predominant part of these decisions were published in the Official Gazette. And practically all of these decisions were carefully drafted. So how can you say that strucna sluzba or technical service showed negligible attitude toward performance of their duties? But do you believe that the members of the technical service or workers and functioners of the technical service were in charge of preparing the decisions of the Crisis Staff? Who initiated decisions which were adopted by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I mentioned that technical services were negligent in the performance of their duty, I meant in legal terms. Technical services would sometimes allow discussion on the issues which were not within the competence of the organs that discussed them. And these decisions could not be adopted as such. When decisions were adopted, they were never precisely worded. At the meetings of the Crisis Staff, the job was never completed and decisions were never signed. We would get feedback from the technical services. After discussion would take place at the Crisis Staff and something was concluded, then such a decision would be worded by the technical services, who would then type it and deliver it to the president for signing. The minutes from the meetings should have been made available to all the participants, but in my case, I never saw any of the minutes, and I never saw the wording of the -- either the Crisis Staff or the Municipal Assembly. I only saw those decisions which were relative to my secretariat because I received them through the protocol, either me or one of my assistants. If those decisions were relative to a certain area, be it the economy, the budget, or service industries, or agriculture. I just wanted to say that the ignorance of people who should have been more professional in their approach to their work and in the channelling of the work of both the Crisis Staff and the Municipal Assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, so you believe that due to the negligence of the technical service, lack of the professionalism within the technical service, some decisions or enactments of the Crisis Staff never were -- which were taken by the Crisis Staff never were formulated and put on the paper and sent to all members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Minutes were never delivered to us, and so that was also the case with the decisions. So we didn't have the feedback on the things that we discussed at our meetings. We didn't have the feedback either in the forms of the minutes or decisions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You just said, and it's page 33: "When decisions were adopted, they were never precisely worded, and they were discussed by the strucna sluzba." So these decisions which were strictly worded, what kind of decision? Can you give us an example?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't understand your question. What is your question? Could you please repeat it? What would you like me to tell you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: My question is: You said that due to the negligence of the technical service, there were discussions and the decisions -- some decisions were never adopted. And in some cases, the decisions were not worded properly or precisely. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the Crisis Staff meetings themselves, decisions were never worded to lend themselves to voting. They were never delivered to the members of the Crisis Staff beforehand. So we never knew what would be discussed at the meetings. Only after discussion on the issues proposed either by the president or one of the members of the Crisis Staff, decisions were drafted subsequently. It would only be natural for us to receive all the necessary materials before the meetings of the Crisis Staff so as to enable us to prepare ourselves for discussions. This would have enabled us to give our remarks and participate in the discussion. That is what I wanted to say. So after the discussions at the meetings of the Crisis Staff, it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. was the technical services that worded or drafted those decisions based on their notes that they took during the meetings. They would then draft the decisions, deliver them to the president for his signature. And as for me, I would only receive those decisions that were relative to the work of my body. I never had an opportunity to see any of the other decisions, and that is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: My next question: Was it possible that Crisis Staff adopted a decision and technical service will never formulate this decision in terms of legal -- in terms -- in proper legal form and presented it to the other members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't get the text in advance for any of the decisions. That's why we didn't know anything about that part. In our work, we did not receive beforehand the decision that we were going to discuss and the decision we were going to adopt at the meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Well, it's -- okay. Let us put the thing another way. A member of the Crisis Staff -- at the meeting of the Crisis Staff, a member of the Crisis Staff proposes to adopt a decision, and then a decision is taken. But then technical services is not working on the wording of this decision and this decision is not delivered in written form to other members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the discussion at the Crisis Staff meeting, there was a person who was in charge of making notes of the discussions that took place during the meeting. That person would also make a note of the decision either being taken or rejected. And after the meeting of the Crisis Staff, this decision would be put on paper, would be drafted, and delivered to the president for signature. We did not have this decision drafted beforehand. This decision was drafted based on the notes taken by the person who was in charge of taking those notes. And then the technical services would put that decision into writing, and that decision would be delivered only to those people that had to receive it. So I didn't receive beforehand, before any of the sessions, any of the decisions that I was going to be involved in taking during any of the sessions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I got your point. I would like you to get my point. Was it possible that a decision would be adopted by the Crisis Staff but technical service never will put this decision on the paper? And this decision would be implemented by the, let us say -- by the president of the Crisis Staff by saying to military or police or the civilian authorities that this decision was taken and please do implement this decision?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether this was possible. I didn't receive any such decision. I can only tell you that I had an opportunity to see a decision that the Prosecution showed me during my testimony, and I could only say that that is a decision that I never saw, and that that decision was never discussed at any of the Crisis Staff meetings. This decision was relative to the release of persons from the reception centres or camps. When I gave that testimony, I had an opportunity to see one of those decisions that I had never seen before, and I said then that I had never seen that decision before and that that decision had never been adopted at any of the sessions that I attended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Okay. My next question: Has the Crisis Staff ever adopted confidential decisions?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. How do you mean "confidential"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Well, in the proper term of this word, a decision which had not to be published or announced publicly?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: You mentioned that somebody always took notes during the meetings of the Crisis Staff. Yes. Do you know the name of the person, the name of the recording clerk or notetaker?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember. I said on -- on Friday, I said when I had met most of those people. I think that the secretary of the assembly was usually present at such meetings, and his name was Mr. Baltic. I think it would have been natural for him to take notes and prepare the material for sessions, but I don't know. I'm not sure. I think that he was supposed to do that as the secretary of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware that Mr. Baltic, Dusan Baltic, was the secretary of the assembly. But he was head of the technical service at the same time, yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was the -- its head, the secretary of the Municipal Assembly. That was the exact title. Now, whether he kept record, I don't know. I really can't remember who was the one who took notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Some of his subordinates took notes during the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I can't remember who took notes. I already said that we did not get the copies of the minutes as members of the Crisis Staff, so I do not know who took notes at the Crisis Staff meetings. I know that Mr. Baltic was present, and I suppose that he took some notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And how many meetings of the Crisis Staff you attended personally?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact number. Quite a number of them. I did not attend all of them, but there were more of those sessions that attended than those I didn't. But the exact number, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Of course, I'm not asking you for an exact figure. 5, 10, 20?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a dozen, five, ten. I don't know. I really don't know. But I was present at the majority of those sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And what issues related to your sphere of responsibility were discussed during the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: My secretariat covered four areas of work: Economic -- economy, education, self-service industries, including children's establishments, social work -- welfare centres. Then there was a department with dealt with agriculture and forestry, and another department for budget and finances. So these were the four departments within the secretariat for economy and service industries. With regard to economic issues, that is, the department which covered economy, pursuant to the then statute now and before, it was responsible for preparing the material, information, for the assembly at the Executive Board about the economic situation from the physical volume of the production to the performance to whatever. And to report to the Executive Board through the secretariat and the Municipal Assembly about the economic results achieved. Insofar as service industries are concerned, apart from the major problems in the field of education at that time, because it was the end of the school year, there were also questions such as looking after people who were social cases. There was in Prijedor a centre for parentless children and other people who needed accommodation. That was part of the -- so kindergartens, Creches, the manner of their financing. As for forestry and agriculture, questions concerning harvesting or spring sowing, and harvesting in June predominated. And by and large, the work of inspectorates in that department protecting forests and forest resources. Budget and finances were the things that I was mostly involved in because the budget fell below 50 per cent with reference to a decision that the assembly had adopted regarding the budget for that year. Simply, the payments had practically come to a halt so that the public revenue distribution was very difficult, if there was any. The internal revenue department, the taxation department, they had very few people anyway. And they found it very difficult to levy and collect taxes and dues. And at that time, the inflation was incredibly high so that even the little money that we managed to collect would be devalued in no time. And I was looking for ways and means to protect it. So those were the topics which dominated my work in that office and my work in the Crisis Staff, and of course, the Executive Board.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was your secretariat or the secretariat you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. headed ever initiated any draft decision which was discussed during the meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were such decisions. I can't remember them specifically. But from those areas which are quite broad, there were a number of issues that were prepared in my offices, in my departments, and were then submitted for discussion to either the Crisis Staff or the Executive Board, or rather every head -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Can you recall -- could you recall the most important decision in the economic sphere?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were all -- I mean, I can't remember. I cannot put them really in any order of importance. But in the economic sector, we did not have any special decisions. Rather, this sector, this department for economy, its only task was to monitor economic trends, prepare draft information and submit it to the assembly. It had no possibility to decide on what individual organisations or enterprises would do. That is, that department and this agency was not as a body superior to companies. It was only a body of the assembly which reported to the assembly about economic developments, the physical volume of production, the number of employees, exports, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, has the Crisis Staff ever discussed the issues related to the destruction and looting of property during the war in the Prijedor Municipality? Property is your sphere of responsibility. Yes?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. It is not. Property was within the province of work of the secretariat for property affairs, if that is what you mean. But indubitably, the Crisis Staff at times, when I urged them, would include in their agenda items to discuss the plunder or destruction of property.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So your statement is that the Crisis Staff never discussed the issues related to the looting and destruction of the property?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the contrary. I confirm that it was at my insistence that there would be discussions of those issues. That is, I confirmed that, yes, it was discussed, and I was one of the authors of proposals to discuss the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Now, you remember that you initiated some decisions before the Crisis Staff to be adopted. Yes? Can you tell us about the content of these decisions?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't the author of draft decisions concerning the property of the citizens in the Municipality of Prijedor because that was not within the jurisdiction of my secretariat. This secretariat was called the secretariat for property affairs. And I, as a member of the body -- of that body, of course, knew all that was going on in the town. There were robberies and the looting of shops, destruction of property, and break-ins into apartments. And we also discussed those matters. But that was not my field of work as the secretary of that secretariat. And I remember that we requested and urged those whose chief task that was, and that is the police, to bring in some order and try to prevent the plunder, chaos, and anarchy which had set in, because precisely those who were responsible to prevent it had failed to do that, and these are the police and the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: And whose properties and houses were looted and destructed, plundered in the Prijedor Municipality?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: By and large, those were Muslim houses. But there were also Serb houses which were broken into and plundered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do you know the instances where persons responsible for the looting and destruction of property were punished by the police?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I don't know that because I didn't have the opportunity to find that out. And I think that those agencies which were to investigate those cases and prosecute them did not work properly. In the first place, I mean, the police, the prosecutor's office, if the police had failed to do its job, then of course the prosecutor's office couldn't do its part of the work. I think they didn't work as well as they should have. But that, of course, is my personal opinion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Travar. It is an appropriate time for the break. Trial stays adjourned until 17.30 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: So, Mr. Travar, can you remember any other decisions initiated by your secretariat or by other members of the Crisis Staff, other bodies of the municipality, related to economic sphere, and especially related to the property?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specifically, no, I don't recall any particular decision. If you could show me one, then I could comment on it. But none of them were important. Now, when it comes to property matters, let me clarify it once again: Matters concerning property in the municipality were not under the province of work of my secretariat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Whose responsibility was the issues of property? Wasn't it an economic issue?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretary of the secretariat for property affairs. That was -- this was called for property relations. Mr. Pavicic headed that secretariat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Was the representative of this secretariat appointed as a member of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vojo Pavicic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: I would like the usher to show the witness Exhibit S181. Item 121 of this exhibit on the first page. The decision to declare property that has been abandoned state property.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you want me to read it or...?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or to comment on it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Please do read this decision, the decision itself.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "All abandoned property, moveable and immoveable, that belonged to people who have left the territory of the municipality of Prijedor and persons who have taken part in the armed rebellion is temporarily declared state property and placed at the disposal of the Municipality of Prijedor. Aricle 2" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The municipal secretariat for urban planning, housing, public utilities, and property law affairs and the municipal surveying administration in cooperation with other municipal organs, shall inventory all immoveable property." I am reading Article 2 once again: "The municipal secretariat for urban planning, housing, public utilities, and property law affairs and the municipal surveying administration in cooperation with other municipal organs shall inventory all immoveable property [Land, single-family houses, business premises, farm buildings, et cetera] owned by persons referred to in Article 1 of the present decision. "Article 3: The allocation of property referred to in Article 1 of the present decision shall be regulated by a separate decision of the Municipal Assembly. "Article 4: The present decision shall remain in force until the relevant legal acts in this domain are adopted by the Assembly of the Serbian Republic of BH. "Article 5: The present decision shall come into force on the day of its adoption and shall be published in the Official Gazette of the Municipality of Prijedor."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Mr. Travar, have you been acquainted with this decision before?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly whether at the time I took part in a Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. discussion about this decision, but I can comment on it. It shows that it refers to the secretariat that I spoke about. But I think that this was an attempt to, if possible, prevent further plunder and destruction of that property. But this is the premise or work of another secretariat, so that specifically I cannot know why it was proposed and why it was adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: Do you think from the point of law, was it legal to declare abandoned property -- all abandoned property, including private property, I suppose, state property without consent of the person who was the owner of this property?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not a lawyer by profession, and I cannot say whether at that time it was possible legally or not. And this decision does not fall within the province of work of my secretariat, so that I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VASSYLENKO
utterances.text: But imagine you had a property and you left Prijedor Municipality, and your property was declared state property. What would be your reaction?

utterances.speaker: RANKO TRAVAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'd ask to get my property back legally. I don't know how to comment on it.
